conversation.content: When can I enroll in Medicare and select my coverage? And when can I make changes to my coverage after I've enrolled?

# Medicare Enrollment and Coverage Change Periods

## Initial Enrollment Periods

**Initial Enrollment Period (IEP)**
- 7-month window around your 65th birthday
- Includes: 3 months before your birthday month, your birthday month, and 3 months after
- Also applies if you're under 65 and qualifying due to disability (after 24 months of disability benefits)

**Special Enrollment Period (SEP)**
- Available if you delayed enrollment due to current employer coverage (you or spouse)
- Typically 8 months after employment ends or coverage stops (whichever comes first)

## Annual Change Periods

**Annual Enrollment Period (AEP)** - October 15 to December 7
- Switch from Original Medicare to Medicare Advantage (or vice versa)
- Change Medicare Advantage plans
- Join, drop, or switch Medicare Part D prescription plans
- Changes take effect January 1

**Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period** - January 1 to March 31
- Only for those already in Medicare Advantage
- Switch to a different Medicare Advantage plan
- Drop Medicare Advantage and return to Original Medicare (and join Part D)
- Changes take effect the first of the following month

## Other Special Enrollment Periods

You may qualify for SEPs due to:
- Moving outside your plan's service area
- Losing other coverage
- Qualifying for Extra Help with drug costs
- Moving into/out of a nursing home
- Other specific circumstances

**Tip:** Missing your Initial Enrollment Period may result in late enrollment penalties, so mark your calendar!
